utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good afternoon everybody, and good afternoon to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So all the accused are here. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Vanderpuye. Noticeably absent amongst the Defence teams, Mr. Ostojic, Ms. Nikolic, and Mr. Sarapa, as far as I can see. All right. We have an oral decision to start with, and then I'll ask you if you have any preliminaries afterwards. The Trial Chamber is seised of the Nikolic motion for certification of the further decision on Prosecution's motion to admit evidence in rebuttal and to reopen its case, filed confidentiality on 30th March, in which he seeks certification to appeal the Trial Chamber's said decision which was filed confidentially on the 27th of March pursuant to the Rule 73(b). The Prosecution filed its response on 30th March arguing that the certification should be denied as the criteria set forth in Rule 73(b) are not met. The Trial Chamber notes the limited scope and nature of the proposed Stevanovic testimony which has been restricted to two issues: First the 2nd battalion's possession of a code book or otherwise; and secondly, the training and capacity of the 2nd Battalion to code and decode telegrams. These are issues, that though important, are of minor significance to the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings and the outcomes of the trial. Furthermore, granting certification would lengthen and not materially advance the proceedings in these final stages of the trial. For these reasons, leave to exceed the word limit is granted, but the motion is denied. Okay. Any preliminaries? There will be a few things that we will refer to you at the end of the sitting about motions and other filings that have arrived in the meantime. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, good afternoon to you and Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to apprise the Court that I did make the witness aware of the limitation concerning the scope of his testimony in advance of his -- well, this afternoon, earlier this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And I also understand that he does not -- has not asked for any protective measures --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Vanderpuye please speak into the microphone, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President, he has not asked for any protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And there is no case for any caution or anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There is not, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's bring Mr. Stevanovic in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're most welcome to this Tribunal and to this trial where you are going to give evidence. Before you start your evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration to the effect that you will be testifying the truth. Madam Usher is going to give you the text of the declaration, please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn making with us. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Vanderpuye, who I suppose you have already met, will be putting some questions to you. He will then be followed by one or more members of the Defence teams on cross-examination. Mr. Vanderpuye, please make sure that you restrict yourself to the parameters of the Court's ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you and Your Honours, again. Good afternoon to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you, Mr. Stevanovic. We have met before. As you know, my name is Kweku Vanderpuye, and I will put some questions to you relative to a few limited issues. If there is any question that I put to you that you don't understand or is unclear, please let me know and I will rephrase the question or restate it in a way that we can better understand one another. Just for the record, could you please state your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stevanovic, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us a little bit about your military history. Did you complete compulsory service with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did my military service in 1988 in Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what work were you assigned to do during the course of that military service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was trained in telegraphy. After that I was in the soldiers' club. And for a while I worked on the switchboard, the telephone switchboard in Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was your position and rank?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, prior to your mobilization to the VRS, did you engage in any communication-related activities, either militarily or in a civilian context?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us when it was that you were mobilized to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was mobilized in early April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And to what unit were you mobilized?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Initially it was a unit of the Territorial Defence, and eventually it became part of the Army of Republika Srpska. Eventually, the 2nd Battalion evolved from that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was your function serving with the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a private through to 1993 -- or, rather, the month of May of 1993 whereupon I was transferred to the communications centre, again as a private.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you remain in your position with the communications centre throughout the war; that is, until you were demobilized?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as a member of the 2nd Battalion's communication unit, can you tell us how many members were part of that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean on a yearly basis, because the number changed from year to year. It was never the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us in 1995 about how many men were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Around eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in 1995 what was your position in the communications unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was commander of the communications squad from mid-May onwards, I was a komandir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in 1995 did the 2nd Battalion's communications unit have a code book or what we've called in court on occasion a Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not have a code book, but we did have a Razgovornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, when you say a Razgovornik, what do you mean? Could you describe what it is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a document of some four to five sheets of paper containing codes for certain meanings. You were looking for meaning in that. It was for signification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was it a document that was used in connection with communications concerning combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Vanderpuye, try to avoid leading questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was it used for any other purpose, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't use it for any other purposes. There was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of its use concerning combat, was that in relation to communications from any particular unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it had to do with communication between our units out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you say "communication with our units out in the field," do you mean the units of the battalion, the company's, or do you mean -- well, just tell us exactly what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I meant the units that were detached from the Battalion and were out of the area of responsibility of our battalion. It was used for their mutual communication and their communication with the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the Razgovornik that was -- that the 2nd Battalion communications unit had, from where was it obtained?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: We got it from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that Razgovornik or the information communicated to units within the battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: We received them from the brigade and would keep them with us. Whenever we went out into the field, we would take a copy with us and a copy would be left behind in the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did the Razgovornik that you had in the 2nd Battalion communications unit, did it ever change, or did it remain the same?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Periodically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell us what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Every two to three months, not that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what specifically changed during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The codes in that document, the Razgovornik, would change.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did the 2nd Battalion communications unit maintain a Razgovornik in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you maintain the Razgovornik as you've described it in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have one prior to July of 1995 as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where was it kept in the communications unit in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember where in the communications centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a desk with the switchboard console on, and then there was a drawer in that desk where we kept the codes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that drawer accessible to all the members of the unit or was it accessible only to a few members of the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was accessible to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when the Razgovornik was changed, was it kept in the same place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us who was responsible for receiving the Razgovornik when it changed from the brigade, to whom did it go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: There was not an individual who was specifically charged with that. The document would be received from the brigade in the command in some way, through a courier perhaps, and we would keep it with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now -- I'm sorry, the Razgovornik that you had, you said that you used it to derive meanings, and you've described it as a code. Can you tell us how it worked.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Razgovornik contained text that would reflect an order or a request. There would be a set of codes indicating what sort of text or which sort of codes needed to be used for which sort of meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have in e-court please, 65 ter 4465. 3893, I'm sorry. If we could just go to page 2 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I wonder if you could, I know you've had an opportunity to see this document before, if you could tell us what, for example, the table on the right shows where you see indicated numbers and certain letters.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the code table for radio communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to the numbers and letters that are indicated on the right-hand side, is this a fair approximation of the Razgovornik or the information that was contained in the Razgovornik in the 2nd Battalion, not in substance but in terms of form?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in terms of reading the Razgovornik, does this table operate in principle similarly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell us how so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, if we need letter D, we will write B7, A8.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just blow this up on the screen to the letter table so that we have that. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, I made a mistake. B7, A0 is what we will say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that indicates the letter D; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could this table be used, for example, to spell out text, an order or request as you've indicated in the way that you've described?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did that function in principle similarly to the way the 2nd Battalion's Razgovornik did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go down the page, please. Here you can see what's entitled a signals table, tablica signala, and it says "Soca" on it. Can you tell us what this represents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a signals table where you would look for a meaning, 293 means they are sitting in a meeting. And it was on this basis that one would put a piece of text together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did the Razgovornik that you had at the 2nd Battalion function in a similar way as depicted here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: There were parts that were similar to this, but the Razgovornik contained integral bodies of text.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could please have in e-court 65 ter 4467. I think we have also an English translation of it, but perhaps it's best if we stick with this one for the moment so the witness can ... okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is a document that represents code tables, and it's indicated at the top -- if we could go to the top. Razgovornik Jablan it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what this represents to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Razgovornik, the code table we used in the field for radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this distinguished or distinguishable from the Razgovornik that you described that the 2nd Battalion communications unit had in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is very similar in form, in format.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does this Razgovornik contain integrated -- the integrated text that you refer to that the 2nd Battalion's Razgovornik had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In what way, if you could just give us an example by reading out one of the phrases or one of the codes corresponding to the phrase?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In order for us to receive the following message, we attacked the unit along the right-hand side, we would say A38, B24, A.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could just blow that up a little bit, it will be on the left-hand side, first box. All right. Now, the record reflects that you said "A38, B24." Did you mean B26.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you just read that out so that -- since we don't have a translation before us, just read out what 4(a) says.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: "We attacked with the unit along the right axes."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you tell us what 4(b) says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Along the left axes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did this function in a similar way to the Razgovornik that you had in the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the top of this box on the left-hand side it reads "Information;" is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where it says Obavestenje, at the top?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And next to that it reads "order."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we can go to the further right --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In e-court, please. All the way to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It reads "Requirements and terms;" is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Requirements and terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you to read A34.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: A34, if I -- and I can't see which one was it in B26, because the B column we looked at initially also had to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could zoom out a little bit just so that the witness can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us how you would code, for example, item number 4 under "Requirements and Terms," which is coded 34 on your right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that would read what, just so that we are clear on the record?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: "We defined or determined the medical station for axes."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now if we could go to the very last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in this document you see three Razgovorniks, one is indicated Jablan, the other is Kesten, and the other is Javor. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and then there are numbers next to each. 1-10, 11-20, and 21-31.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: This means that from day 1 to day 10 in a month, the Jablan code was used; from 11 to 20, the Kesten code was used; and from day 21 to day 31, Javor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did the Razgovornik that you had in the 2nd Battalion function in a similar way in terms of limiting duration to a period of time in a month or period of time within a day, day or night, for example?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It referred to either the period of day 1 to day 10, or from day 11 to day 20, or day 21 to day 31. Depending on the date various code tables or Razgovornik were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, in July 1995 did you personally know how to use the Razgovornik that was kept by the 2nd Battalion communications unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us when and where you were taught how to use a Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was trained by my colleagues who took me in, in 1993 when I first came to the communications centre. I underwent some training during my regular military service earlier on. That was how I learned how to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you as a komandir of the communications unit, I think you said from May on in 1995, did you provide any training to the members of your unit as to how to use your Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Whoever asked me to show them how it was used, I did. I couldn't force anyone to learn this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And given what you've demonstrated to us today and your experience in the unit, how much training would you say is required in order to learn how to use a Razgovornik, particularly the one that you had in the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were there members of the battalion, 2nd Battalion communications unit that knew how to use the Razgovornik besides you in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many other members of the unit knew how to use the Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, between two and three.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And who are those individuals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ilic could use it very well, Pisic, as well as Peric.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were any of these individuals trained by you on how to use the unit's Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you know, how did they acquire the knowledge to use a Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I showed the system, how it worked to Peric, and I think it took me only 15 minutes to do that. I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you aware of any other deciphering tables, books, or devices that were possessed by the 2nd Battalion communications unit in order to decode or code telegrams?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were there any other deciphering tables, books, or devices that were used by the 2nd Battalion or maintained by the 2nd Battalion command in order to decode or code telegrams?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The communications centre, no. And in July 1995 I learned that the code tables were -- was held at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say that it was held in the -- held at the command, can you tell us by whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The battalion command. We did not have any means to access that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Stevanovic. I don't have any further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We've had an occasion to meet two days ago, but just for the record let me introduce myself to you again. My name is Zoran Zivanovic, and I represent Mr. Vujadin Popovic in these proceedings. I am going to have just a few questions for you. Could you please tell me how often did you use this Razgovornik in your communication between the battalion command and the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Almost not at all, almost never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me why do you say not at all? Did you have any other means of communication? Was there any other communication that was safe enough to transmit some confidential conversations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a high-quality wire induction communication line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, for the purpose of the record, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Stephane Bourgon, and this afternoon I am accompanied with my colleague Ms. Marie-Josee Barry-Gosselin, and together we represent Drago Nikolic in these proceedings. I have a few questions I would like to ask you this afternoon. And as my colleague put it to you, if there is any question that you do not understand, please do not hesitate to interrupt me and to ask me to say the question over again so that we are proceeding on a sound basis. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have a few questions I would like to begin with before I look into the questions that I had prepared for you, simply, as a follow-up to what my colleague asked you from the Prosecution. My first question is that you mention at page 5, lines 23 to 24, that you were the commander of the communications centre within the 2nd Battalion. And my first question is simply: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber to what extent -- to what extent, sorry, you were the komandir of the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: To the extent of being in charge of the technical part of the job rather than of the military part of the job; in other words, I did not have the power to issue orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So could I use the term that you were something like the first among equals? Would be a term that you would be familiar with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, today at page 5, line 25, to page 6, lines 1 and 2, in response to a question put to you by my colleague, you said that you had a Razgovornik within the 2nd Battalion but that you had no code book. Can you explain the difference between a code book and a Razgovornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A Razgovornik has a textual part whereas the code book does not have that part. A code book is an entirely different document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And was there a code book at the 2nd Battalion, whether in the battalion command or in the battalion communications centre, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, one night the commander showed me where it was, where the code book was, when I was at the command -- actually, not just to me, he'd showed that place to all the members of the command. I, myself, did not see it. I never perused it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, also today in response to a question that was put to you by my colleagues, you stated - I don't have the exact page number - but you stated that there were no other documents beside the Razgovornik that was kept and maintained at the 2nd Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct that the communications centre did not have it. I did not know of any other documents before July. I can't even be sure of any other thing today, because I can remember only a piece of paper that was hanging on the wall and that the commander pointed to me. I never read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, we will come back to this topic, but I would like to address very quickly something you mentioned in an interview you had with the Prosecution on the 3rd of February of this year. Do you remember this interview with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And during this interview, you stated that you had one opportunity where you were called to the battalion command and you were asked to decode a telegram; do you recall saying something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you tell us why you were not able to decode that telegram on that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Because it could not be decoded with use of the Razgovornik. The terms in the telegram did not correspond to the terms in the Razgovornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So basically what you are telling me is that you needed the code book in addition to the Razgovornik in order to be able to decode that telegram, and you did not have the book; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, first it's a compound question. And the second thing is that the witness had previously stated it, so it's a mischaracterization of his previous testimony as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, I take it that the witness knows exactly what he would have said or what he said when he was interviewed. And secondly, if he's got a problem with the question, if he thinks it's complicated, he can ask us to divide it into two parts. And I don't think it is. So if you can answer the question, please proceed, Mr. Stevanovic. If you need help, let us know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer the question. However, not with the Razgovornik. That part had to be excluded, because you could not do anything with just the Razgovornik. One would have had to have the code book in order to deal with the situation at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the second part of the question there is did not have this code book at the communications centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And until your commander showed you that night something on the wall, you had no knowledge that the 2nd Battalion had such a code book; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And what your commander showed you on the wall that night, you did not have an opportunity to see if it was the missing code book; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, you said earlier on that you never had an opportunity to peruse this code book, and this is a follow-up question which seeks confirmation of this. In other words, that you never had the opportunity to see if this was the missing code book; is that correct? Because you never saw it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true, I never saw it, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You also said to the Prosecution that the companies of the 2nd Battalion also had a Razgovornik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But the companies of the 2nd Battalion did not have the missing code book. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say that. However, since there was none to be had at the communication centre, then I suppose that the other commanders did not have it either. But that's just my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if that coded telegram was sent to the companies, they would not have been able to decode the telegram exactly for the same reason that you were not able to decode the telegram; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, unless they had the code book.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And as you say, in your opinion, they did not have this code book?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's my opinion, but I can't be sure of that. I can't say for a fact that they did or that they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. And now I move, sir, to some of the questions that I had prepared for you today. And first thing I would like to ask you to confirm is that you did meet with the Prosecution for the first time on 24 September, 2009; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I apologise, it's 2008. It's been brought to my attention. So it would have been September 2008; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: 2008, in September, I'm not sure of the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I did the same mistake, so don't worry, sir. And the second time you met with the Prosecution would have been on the 3rd of February for the interview that was conducted by the investigator Tomasz Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, according to the information I have, this information -- this interview was conducted in a car. And I'd be very interested to learn why this interview had to be conducted in a car and not in a normal place.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was my wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And was there a reason for this, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, sir, the next time you met with the Prosecution was the following day, on the 4th of February, and you were again asked some questions by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the next time you met with the Prosecution was on 23rd and 24th of March 2009 when you met on the first day with the investigator, Tomasz; and the second day with my colleague from the Prosecution, Mr. Vanderpuye. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, on the first day, that is the 23rd of March, you had the opportunity to review the transcript of your 3 February interview. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you confirm on that occasion that what was contained in the interview was accurate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: There was just two details.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We'll come to those details, but one of those details was the date upon which you would have received the coded telegram at the 2nd Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And what was the second -- I don't recall, what was the second thing, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the Serbian version, a sentence was interrupted. It was not finished; whereas, in the English it appeared as being finished. I'm talking about my answers to the questions put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you recall the question? If not, maybe we will get to it as we go in the questioning.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, on the 24th of March when you met with my colleague, Mr. Vanderpuye, again you had the opportunity to review the transcript of your 3 February interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And other than for the same two discrepancies, you confirm that the interview was accurate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have an occasion to see the transcript of the last interview. If the interview was on the 3rd, and on the 4th I did not have the occasion to see the transcript of the interview which took place on the 4th. I only listened to the audiotape, and it was not on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But the audiotape, which was the interview of the 3rd of February, it was accurate other than for the date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, would I be right in saying -- or, maybe I can ask this in a different manner: How long did your meeting with the Prosecution last on the 24th of March; your proofing session, how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It would have been about two or three hours, but I'm not sure. You are talking about the second meeting with them?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, I am talking actually the meeting with my colleague Mr. Vanderpuye on the 24th of March, when you were here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you can confirm that you and I did have the opportunity of meeting yesterday.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that on that occasion I did show you in your language a translated version of the notes that were given to us by the Prosecution after the proofing session. Do you recall me showing this to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, at the end of this document, there is a mention that you met with a member of the Nikolic Defence on two occasions. Can you confirm that those two occasions, one was actually a meeting and one was a telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you confirm that the first meeting took place after your first meeting with the Prosecution on 24 September, 2008?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was in December 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you confirm that the telephone conversation took place after the interview that was conducted by the investigator Tomasz with yourself on the 3rd of February?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the only time you and I met was yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I suggest to you, sir, that the reason why we did not travel to see you before the Prosecution is because we were -- we obtained information that on 14 and 15 July, 1995, you were not present at the 2nd Battalion command. Can you confirm this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can't confirm the date, but I can confirm the days. On Thursday, after 2100 hours I was not present at the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, this is exactly what I would like to explore at this point in time. And I'd like for this purpose to show you the transcript of your interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Which, if I can have in e-court, please, and that would be 3D00566.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, I will show you -- this transcript will appear in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I would like to have in B/C/S page 1 and in English also page 1, please. And maybe I have the wrong number. I apologise, it's 3D00567, which is the interview of 3 February. I mixed up the six and the seven, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, I draw your attention in your language to lines 18 to 24, and the same can be found at the bottom of page 1 in English, lines 27. And then we will have to go to page 2 for line 1 for the final word of what I would like to read to you. So I'll just read that question, and I ask you, sir, that you read that in your own language. TB, this is Tomasz Blaszczyk, I hope I am getting the pronunciation right with his name. But he says: "Q. Okay, and you indicated a few minutes ago, and I ask you also again about your knowledge about event from July 1995, and I asked you whether you were called to the Brigade, to the Battalion HQ in regard to the coded telegram. "A. Yes. "Q. And you told me that you were called. Is it correct? "A. Yes." That's the part that is on the next page in English. Sir, do you recall having been asked those questions and giving these answers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you mention to the investigator here that you were called to the Battalion HQ in regards to a coded telegram, I take it that this was before the beginning of the real interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'll try to make it more clear, and I appreciate when you do that so I have an opportunity to make it clear. According to the text that we have before us, at lines 18 to 24, and that's the beginning of the interview, Mr. Blaszczyk asked you a few minutes ago: "I ask you about your knowledge about an event in July 1995, and you told me that you were called at the Battalion HQ, and you confirmed that." What I would like to know is that when Mr. Blaszczyk put that question to you, that was before he put the tape on to start recording?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And how many questions were put to you before the tape was put on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the questions pertaining to that part -- actually, there were not that many. There were -- most of the questions were about going to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So the questions about going to the command, there were a few questions or many questions before the tape was placed at on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: A few, not many.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Blaszczyk put that -- those questions to you, those few questions, he did not tell you which coded telegram he was referring to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So when he put that question to you before the tape was put in function, he did not tell you that he was referring to any telegram ordering the 2nd Battalion to put together a group of its soldiers to participate in the execution of prisoners. He never mentioned that to you before placing the tape at on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but he also asked me whether I knew anything about a coded telegram that arrived in July. This is what he said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But he didn't tell you anything about the content of that telegram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you were answering the questions put to you by Mr. Blaszczyk concerning the existence of a coded telegram, you did not know what was the content of the telegram he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of the content of the telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So all you knew at the time is that you had received one coded telegram in July of 1995, and, you, yourself, you knew that you never found out the content of this telegram; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to move to page 4 of the interview in B/C/S, and I believe it's page 5 in English. Sorry, it's also page 4 in English. So in English it would be 30 to 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in your language, sir, it would be lines 8 to 11. So I will read it in English. "Q. Okay. This everything happened you said in July 1995. "A. Yes. "Q. It was sometime about Wednesday, Tuesday, or Monday? "A. It had to be before Wednesday." Do you recall saying this, sir? Sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I would like to show you another exhibit while we keep this on the screen, and I would like the court usher to give it to you in paper, and that is 6D196, and I do have a paper copy to give to the judges, and I've already given a copy on this side of the courtroom. And I will give a copy to the Prosecution simply because I will be referring to this exhibit quite a bit, and it's better if we have it in our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If that's okay with my colleague, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, you can confirm that what I just gave you or what the court usher just gave you is the calendar for July of 1995. Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So when you said during the interview "before Wednesday ..." what you actually meant is before 12 July. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, if you go down and look back again on the screen for the interview at lines 12 to 15, and for the English it's page 5, lines 7 to 10, if I have the right. Sorry, in English it would be line 1 up until line 4. And it reads as follows. Tomasz Blaszczyk: "Okay, I understand, but it was after the fall of Srebrenica?" And your answer was: "We did not know about the fall of Srebrenica, we were not informed. We did not have any information, and we did not know what was going on till maybe some times Wednesday, Thursday, probably." So my question is, looking back at the calendar I just gave you, this would mean that you found out about the fall of Srebrenica on the 12th or the 13th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm looking at the calendar. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But that coded telegram you say was received by the 2nd Battalion, that was before the 13th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I also understand from your interview that when you would have received or when a coded telegram would have been received at the 2nd Battalion, you were not aware at the time that there were prisoners of war in the area of Rocevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, we can also read this answer which is part of your interview, and that was page 5, lines 7 to 15 in English, and in B/C/S page 4 lines 18 to 24. Sir, would you agree with me that the presence of prisoners of war is something that you learned later on Monday or Tuesday [Realtime transcript read in error "Tuzla"] of the following week when you returned home after the battle of Baljkovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if we look again at the calendar that you have, and of course that's 6D196 for the record, so this would be on the 17th or the 18th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what the reference to the 17th or the 18th of July is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry, there is a correction I need to do in the transcript on page 30, line 2. I thank my colleague for that, the word "Tuzla" appeared and it should be "Tuesday," Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, I will say my question again. In the interview you said that you found out about the presence of prisoners of war in Rocevic when returning home on the Monday or the Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So what Monday and Tuesday are you referring to on this calendar? What date is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to have in e-court now a different document, which is the supplemental information sheet of 26th March, and the number I have here is 3D00569.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, this is the written version of the notes which were given to us by the Prosecution after they met with you. And I draw your attention to the fifth paragraph, those are numbers that were added by the Defence, Mr. President, simply for the sake of being able to go faster. So the fifth paragraph, and it reads here: "The witness added that the events concerning the coded telegram occurred not later than 13 July 1995." Can you confirm that indeed -- or, sorry, I have to make my questions more clear. If I look at this paragraph here, I'd like to know which one is it. Earlier you said it had to be before 13 July, and in here, in the information sheet, you said "... not later than 13 July." So can you help us with a more precise answer. Is it no later than 13 July, or is it before 13 July as you said in the interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not after the 13th of July because at 2100 hours on Thursday, I was not in the communications centre. I was not there. That's the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So in other words the telegram you say would have been received at the 2nd Battalion command could not have been received on the 13th of July because you were not there. Is that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, can you explain to us why it is not possible that you received that -- that the telegram coded was received on that day; in other words, where were you on 13th July in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: The telegram I received could not have been received after 2100 hours on Thursday because on that evening I set out for Standard, and from there on to Maricici since we were supposed to protect the city from Muslim forces advancing towards Baljkovica and threatening to break through the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I can have in e-court and in B/C/S just the next page so we can cover the sixth paragraph. In English I think we have the right place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that you did in July of 1995 receive a wedding invitation which you were supposed to attend on Sunday, the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And as you just mention, in the evening of 13 July you were sent to Standard. Can you confirm that you went there along with a group of about 30 soldiers? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that I was a part of a group of some 20-30 men. I'm not sure of the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And what time did you depart from the lines of the 2nd Battalion to go to Standard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: At around 9.00 p.m. on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And from Standard, would you agree that after waiting some time there, you were then taken to Maricici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Did you notice any units, any other units present along with your group in Maricici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was either a company or a platoon of the military police from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you recall who was in command of the group you were part of on the evening and night of 13 to 14 July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That evening it was Ljubo Bojanovic who took us out to the front lines. He was probably in command of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you recall during that evening or during that night from 13 to 14 July whether you saw Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the night, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When did you see Dragan Obrenovic, if you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him on Friday as he was getting past us and said that nobody should stop us, or something along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any time that's convenient for you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: About two more questions, Mr. President, then we will -- then I can move on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, if I look, you just mentioned Friday, so you saw Dragan Obrenovic on the 14th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in the proofing note that you have before you on the screen, and that is in the bullet number 6 or the sixth paragraph, you mention there what Dragan Obrenovic said. Can you read what you mentioned to the Prosecution and confirm whether this is correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: He said that "Nobody should stop these people," and he meant the Muslims, in other words, he wanted them to be released, to be let go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's a translation issue, but did he say "Nobody should stop them," or "Nobody can stop them"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Nobody can stop them," that's what he said. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you -- do you recall that with this group you ended up in Baljkovica on Saturday the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when did you return to the lines of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I returned to the lines of the 2nd Battalion only some two or three days after I got back home. I took some time to rest. I don't recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when did you return? When did this group of soldiers that were deployed from the 2nd Battalion, when did the group return as a group to the 2nd Battalion? What day or what date, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that. These were company men, and it depended on individuals companies, when they would allow their men to go on leave. I remember that I got there again some two or three days after I got back from Baljkovica. I wouldn't be able to tell you about the other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Maybe let me make that more clear. When did you return home after Baljkovica, you, yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I returned home on Tuesday. I think it was a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And according to the calendar, this would be around the 18th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, we can go for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, we'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, when we left before the break, we were discussing the fact that you were deployed with a group of soldiers from the 2nd Battalion initially to Standard and then to Maricici in Baljkovica. My first question is --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- do you remember any other members of the 2nd Battalion who were with you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: There was Milan Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Anybody else that you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I can't be certain, but I know for a fact that Milan was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir, when we met you mentioned a name, Savo Acimovic. Do you recall mentioning this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you recall if he was there also, or you can't be sure?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I recall him being there, but he was killed. That's why I didn't mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's a very good reason. I'm sorry. Now, Milan Radic who was with you testified before this Trial Chamber, and I quote quickly from page 26162, at lines 13 and 14, and in response to a question he said: "I said that I left approximately on the 13th and that I came back on the 16th or the 17th, which means that I spent five days in the field." Sir, does that correspond to the dates that you would have deployed with this group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, save for the return date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Which would be, according to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That would have been the 18th, the Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, there was a statement which was provided by Milan Radic which was admitted in evidence, and I would like to quote part of this statement. And that is from 3D00457, and Milan Radic said in this statement: "In July 1995 after the fall of Srebrenica, I cannot remember the exact date, the battalion commander ordered me to prepare 12 soldiers from my company to go in the field on the front line. As I only managed to provide 11 soldiers, the battalion commander ordered me to go with them as the twelfth soldier." Sir, is this information that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When did you become aware of this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I learned this on the day of our departure. The commander said that he would go unless he would be able to collect as many men as were required.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the statement goes on: "That same procedure took place in the other two companies as well, and so one platoon of about 36 soldiers had been formed." Do you recall whether soldiers from the two other companies also were part of that group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were. I don't know how many, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And his statement continues: "As far as I remember, that platoon headed towards Snagovo on 13 July," but he says in the afternoon. "In the evening we arrived to the Maricici position, where we spent the night of 13 to 14 July 1995." Does that correspond of the information as to your deployment as you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: It does, save for the fact that we set out in the evening and not in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And he goes on to describe: "We also remained there, that is in Maricici, the following day and one more night. On 15 July, 1995, around 11.00 a.m., we left that position in Maricici. There were no combat activities with the BiH Army in that region. The ABiH broke through our lines and left towards Baljkovica. On 15 July 1995, when we left the position in Maricici, I thought we were going back to the battalion; however, the order was to continue towards Baljkovica where we arrived in the afternoon. We were immediately deployed along the front line. Those two days were very hard. There were heavy combats until 16 July 1995 when the corridor was open and the Muslim forces crossed the defence line. "After the corridor was opened, we went through the woods towards Ceparde, and we stayed three more days in Ceparde. We could not go back towards Zvornik since Crni Vrh was closed. Three days later we returned to the battalion." Does that correspond to the situation as you lived through it in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, save for some minor details.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Like which ones?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, for example, that already on the morning of Sunday my unit was divided. The Muslims forces divided it into two parts, one was left in the direction towards the headquarters and the other one towards Caparde. We were retreating towards the woods. That's where they were driving us. He said that we stayed there for three days, that means Sunday, Monday, and on Tuesday we headed back. Since Crni Vrh was closed off, the agreement was that the -- their rear forces and the units of the Muslim army that were left behind would be leaving the area, passing through.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Ljubo Bojanovic, whom you referred to earlier, he testified in the Blagojevic case, and his testimony was admitted in this case. At page 11710 to 11714 in the Blagojevic case, I mention this more for my colleague than for you, sir, he testified at around 2.00 a.m. during the night from 13 to 14 July he was ordered to take forces from Standard to Maricici. Is this information you can relate to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I said that Ljubo Bojanovic was most probably the commander of the unit since he was the one to take us out to Maricici and deploy us there. As for the time, I can't claim with any precision whether it happened a day earlier or a day -- or an hour earlier or an hour later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know somebody by the name of Cvijetinovic, I think his name was mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Cvijetinovic testified in this case, and this is what is -- this is what he said. At page 25854 to 25855, lines 18 to first line on the next page: "Okay. You know someone named Dragan Stevanovic?" His answer was: "Yes." "Q. Who was he? "A. He was the commander of the communications section. "Q. Commander of the communications section, was he working on the 14th of July of 1995? "A. No. "Q. Are you sure about that?" "A. No, no." My question is: Were you at the 2nd Battalion command on 14 July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a question that you put to me? I was there until 9.00 p.m., 8.00 or 9.00 p.m. when set out for Standard on the 14th -- or, rather, no, sorry, on the 13th. And on the 14th, no. In other words, I was there on Thursday until 9.00 p.m., and on Friday I wasn't there. I had, by that time, reached Maricici.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I can have in e-court, please, P00312.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, this is the attendance roster for the 2nd Battalion command for July of 1995. My first question is: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I draw your attention to line number 1 towards the end of the document where we see your name. Do you see this at line 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And it says here for the dates of 13-19, I see the following letters: 13 plus, 14 plus, 15 -- it's difficult to tell, but it appears to be something like a 3. In English it's not there, but we have a V. And then 16 says T, 17 says T, 18 and 19 also say T. Sir, on the basis of this report, it would appear that you were at the Battalion command on 13 and 14. Can you explain this.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, but I wasn't there. I've already told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now I -- it's just to confirm, and I just -- and I can understand that. But so that would be a mistake, or how would those letters be there on this report saying that you were there on the 13th and the 14th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have to ask the person who was keeping the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you recall who was keeping this record?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that it was Lazarevic and Jovic, they were in charge of the personnel affairs, but I wouldn't know who exactly was in charge of keeping the records. I don't know which of the two might have done that. I don't know what the two of them actually did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, sir, I draw your attention to the next -- to line 4 in the same section, where it says Cvijetinovic. Do you see this, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, under the date 13 July, it says OD, Oscar-Delta. What does that mean, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you confirm --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Or on furlough, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And are you aware that on 13 July Cvijetinovic was not in the command of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you happen to know where he was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: He was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And for 14 July, we have a plus. What does that mean, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That he was present; however, I don't remember when he arrived. On the 13th, if --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness could repeat what happened on the 13th --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe he arrived in the afternoon, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And sir, does this roster that appears before you, does that change your testimony in any way that the coded telegram you say would have been received at the 2nd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Sorry to interrupt you like this, I hate to do it, Mr. Bourgon, however, it's in the interest of everyone. Line 17, the transcript -- and line 18, actually, of the previous page, we've got a part of the witness's testimony which is completely missing in the transcript. He -- the question was: "Mr. Stevanovic, and for 14 July we have a plus, what does that mean, if you know?" And then you answered: "That he was present; however, I don't remember when he arrived." And then you continued: "On the 13th if ..." But we don't know what you said because we don't have it in the transcript. If you could kindly repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was absent on the 13th. I'm sure of that. He was celebrating. I believe that he did return on the 14th, but I don't know when; therefore, I cannot confirm anything about the 14th. However, I am absolutely positive that he was absent on the 13th. It was his holiday, his religious holiday, and it was common practice to allow people to be absent on their patron saint day, which was, for him, on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I repeat the question that I asked just a little earlier, and that is the roster that appears before you, does that change in any way your testimony that the telegram you say would have been received at the 2nd Battalion command would have been received before 14 July? Does that change this in any way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not changing my statement. The command of the 2nd Battalion did receive the telegram before the Thursday, i.e., before the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know someone by the name of Mitar Lazarevic, and who is he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a command member.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, Mitar Lazarevic testified in this case, and I refer to page 13373 to 13374. He testified about a coded telegram which would have been received at the 2nd Battalion command after midnight on the night of 14 to 15 July. My question is the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just want the record to be clear that the testimony was not equivocal in that respect, and my colleague has characterised it as that Mr. Lazarevic said it would have been received; in fact, he said it was. It just want the record to be clear on that because it is -- it is in fact what the testimony was. My colleague has stated it to this witness as though it's a conditional issue, and it really just isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think Mr. Bourgon would --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just to be clear, we all know Mr. Bourgon's speech and that's the way he speaks and that's what he means, and I think we know that, we just wanted to get it on the record. Many times he says "would have" when I think he means "was."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and I didn't want to say it because I was a little bit -- feel offended, but I know that that is the way he speaks. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Not the first and not the last time, Mr. President. I'm trying to do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, based on what my colleague just said, that Mitar Lazarevic said that the telegram would have been received on -- no, was received on 14 July, my question is the following: Based on your knowledge, would you agree that this certainly cannot be the same telegram, the same coded telegram which would have been received by the 2nd Battalion while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: If he received it on the 14th July, it was a different telegram. If he received it on Friday or during the night between Thursday and Friday, because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, sir, you know who Sreten Acimovic is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Sreten Acimovic also testified in this case, and I refer to page 12944-12945, to my verification there was not closed session, but I stand to be corrected. Sir, he also testified about a coded telegram which was received after midnight between 1.00 and 2.00 a.m. on the night of 14 to 15 July 1995. Sir, it's my understanding based on your testimony that this cannot be the same coded telegram you say would have been received by the 2nd Battalion when you were there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's what you're saying, but what is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My question to you is that do you agree with that, that it cannot be the same telegram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: If it arrived on the 14th, it's not the same telegram. I received the telegram earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you have any knowledge about a coded telegram which would have been received at the second battalion command during the night of 14 to 15 July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And sir, when you return to the 2nd Battalion command after the battle of Baljkovica around the 18th of July, did anyone mention anything to you about a coded telegram which would have been received at the 2nd Battalion command while you were away during the night of 14 to 15 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear anything. I was not there. We never discussed that. Bygones were bygones, life went on and we never discussed anything that happened before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So Sreten Acimovic never discussed a coded telegram with you that would have arrived on 14th July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, we never discussed that. And we knew about the one that I received -- actually, that I was asked to decode.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Mitar Lazarevic never spoke to you or discussed with you a telegram coded that would have been received in your absence on 14 July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did any of the signalmen or communicators in your section discuss with you when you returned a coded telegram which would have been received in your absence on 14 July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did anyone else in the 2nd Battalion discuss with you or mention to you a coded telegram which would have been received in your absence on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STEVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say that anybody did, that anybody discussed the specific telegram of the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, sir, I would like to move to a different section also dealing with the telegram of 14 July. When Mitar Lazarevic testified - and that was on page 13374 - he said the following: "Q. Okay. Tell us about this telegram that arrived. "A. The telegram arrived, and in that telegram it was requested that a group of people would be sent to Rocevic to execute these men. The telegram was coded."
